hints: Focus on how buta-1,3-diene adds, the two C=C bonds do not both stay intact in 1,4-addition.

Draw the monomer as $\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2$ and join C1 to C4 through the chain, leaving just one C=C in the middle of the repeat unit $-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2-$.
For cis, the two continuing chain bonds must be on the same side of that remaining double bond, so look for the U-shaped repeat unit rather than the zig-zag one.
walkthrough:
**Draw the monomer**

Think of buta-1,3-diene simply as two alkenes joined together.

$$\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2$$
Addition polymerisation breaks pi bonds to make new sigma bonds to the next monomer.

**Do 1,4-addition**

The normal rubber-like polymer uses C1 and C4 to link to neighbours. Both outer pi bonds open, the middle becomes one C=C.

$$\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2 \rightarrow -\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2-$$
So the correct repeat unit must contain four carbons with only one double bond in the centre.

**Apply cis meaning**

Cis means the two bulky groups on a C=C are on the same side. Here the two bulky groups are the two $-\text{CH}_2-$ chain continuations.
In cis, both chains bend to the same side of the double bond, giving a bent U shape. In trans they point to opposite sides, giving a zig-zag shape.

options.A: Incorrect. This repeat unit still shows two C=C double bonds. Addition polymerisation must break at least one pi bond to link monomers, so a 1,4-addition product can only retain one C=C.
options.B: Incorrect. This shows the correct connectivity $-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2-$ but in the trans arrangement. The chain bonds enter and leave on opposite sides of the double bond, giving the extended zig-zag shape, not cis.
options.C: Correct. This shows $-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2-$ from 1,4-addition with both $\text{CH}_2$ groups on the same side of the C=C. That bent shape is exactly cis, the structure of natural rubber type polybutadiene.
options.D: Incorrect. This shows 1,2-addition, where only one double bond is used and a pendant $\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2$ side group is left. The question asks for the 1,4-addition cis polymer with the double bond in the backbone.
